clue.text: If one's in agreement, one won't come to blows

indicators.note: the words before it are placed in the word for agreement, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a pact is an agreement
taken as written
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A remark that anyone who agrees with you won't start a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'one's' supplies its own letter S after I for one; the definition describes a person who refuses all violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposed to all violence will never take part in a fight.

clue.text: Bird nearly out of breath?

indicators.note: nearly means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: puffing means panting, out of breath

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bird is almost exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter G from PUFFING.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird with a colourful beak, found on northern coasts.

clue.text: Hawking is lamentable

definitions.meaning: street traders cry their wares, calling them out for sale
a ... shame is a deplorable one

explanation.definitionFit: Hawkers call out goods for sale, and 'crying' as an adjective means deplorable.

clue.text: Bouquet for a French king?

parts.note: a bunch of flowers for a monarch suggests itself, but the bouquet is a pleasant smell, and the word splits as if 'for a' plus a name ending in France

explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its pleasing scent or aroma.

clue.text: Chapter in extortionate contract poses hurdles to be overcome

parts.note: a steep price is an extortionate one

indicators.note: the chapter's abbreviation goes in the word for contract

parts.note: a lease is a rental contract

explanation.surface: A clause in an expensive agreement creating obstacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poses' is a link word here, so the definition is the obstacle course itself rather than anything a contract poses.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race over fences and ditches is a course of obstacles to clear.

clue.text: To capture leader in uniform, lots of soldiers all work together

indicators.note: a body that captures something holds it within itself, so the soldiers' word goes round the pick

parts.note: a corps is a large body of troops

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers marching in step and capturing their chief in uniform, all cooperating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To capture' puts U, the first letter given by 'leader in uniform', inside CORPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete body of writings by one author, collected together, is called a corpus.

clue.text: In debt — why unable to fly?

definitions.meaning: having money still due to someone
a bird with O (no) wing cannot fly

explanation.definitionFit: Being behind on payments means money is due, and 'O wing' means having no wing at all.

clue.text: Three men of a saintly sort

parts.note: Pat is a man's name
Ron is a man's name
Al is a man's name

explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a patron saint, as in a church's festival day.

clue.text: They resume wrongdoing, say with dubious poses

indicators.note: say means the word before it is spoken, and its sound is written down

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing

indicators.note: dubious means doubtful or suspect, so the letters are not to be trusted in order

explanation.surface: Criminals returning to crime, posing suspiciously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives SYN as said like SIN, and 'dubious' rearranges POSES into OPSES. 'Resume' is read as a noun (résumé), a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: Short summaries of a text are résumés, here written without accents.

clue.text: Knowing the questions could stop the butterflies

parts.note: fly is an informal word for sharp or knowing
an exam paper is the set of questions

explanation.surface: Seeing the exam questions in advance would calm a student's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butterflies' looks like nervousness, as the surface wants; the definition reads them as insects that a sticky sheet would trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky sheet hung up to trap insects would catch any butterfly that landed.

clue.text: A little marmalade?

parts.note: marmalade here is an orange-coloured cat, and a little one is its young

explanation.definitionFit: A marmalade cat is a ginger tabby, and its young offspring is a small cat of the same colour.

clue.text: Barbados opener, O, held at square leg at Worcester once

indicators.note: the O is held back until after the other pieces, placed at the end
the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
a T-square is a draughtsman's tool, giving T
taken as written
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: the Barbadian opening batsman caught by a fielder at square leg, playing at Worcester's county ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Square leg is a cricket fielding position. Worcester, in 1651, was a battle site of the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The final battle of the English Civil War was fought at Worcester in 1651, so the city was then a field of combat.

clue.text: It's less obvious this man needs food

definitions.meaning: something less obvious lies further in, hidden from view
the idiom of satisfying the '... man' means feeding oneself

explanation.definitionFit: Lying further in makes something less visible, and the idiom 'the inner man' means one's appetite.

clue.text: Repertory company that entertains the children?

definitions.meaning: a troupe that performs plays could be called a ...
a nursery group where young children play under supervision

explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical troupe stages drama, while a preschool session keeps toddlers amused.

clue.text: One of the lower orders ordering a bitter? Never!

indicators.note: ordering the letters means arranging them anew

explanation.surface: A man from the working classes asking for a pint of bitter at the bar, then refusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' rearranges the letters of A BITTER and NEVER. 'Lower orders' sounds like the working class; here it means the lower biological orders.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal without a backbone belongs to a simpler group of creatures in zoology.

clue.text: Last drink — good health!

parts.note: bottom means last in rank
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Calling for a final drink with a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking toast urging everyone to drain their glasses, like 'cheers'.

clue.text: Director sadly is owed money by firm

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who is owed

indicators.note: sadly means unfortunately or badly, so the letters are in poor order

explanation.surface: A company director unhappily discovering the firm owes them money.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender or supplier awaiting payment from a business holds a debt against it.

clue.text: Branch rotten — put on fire

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
to shoot is to fire

explanation.definitionFit: A side growth from a stem or a group splitting from a parent body.

clue.text: Squashes new arrivals in among the rest anyhow

indicators.note: one piece is set in among the letters of the other
anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: freshmen are first-year students newly arrived at university

explanation.surface: Fruit squashes to be shared among newcomers and the remaining guests at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' scrambles the four letters of the word for the remainder so they split around the students; 'the' is padding. Squashes are British fruit drinks, so the definition is a plural noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit drinks served at an event are part of the food and drink offered.

clue.text: Banger bought in Delhi by the sound of it

definitions.text: Banger bought in Delhi by the sound of it

parts.words: Banger bought in Delhi by the sound of it
parts.note: a banger is a sausage, and Delhi said aloud is deli, a delicatessen where cured sausage is sold

explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy cured sausage sold sliced at a delicatessen counter.

clue.text: Cook vegetable that's available

parts.note: beet is a root vegetable
on means available, as a dish on the menu

explanation.surface: An instruction to cook a vegetable that is in season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a verb but is a noun: Mrs Isabella Beeton wrote a famous Victorian British cookery book.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Beeton was a celebrated Victorian writer on cookery and household management.

clue.text: Is he the distributor for The Tablet?

definitions.text: Is he the distributor for The Tablet?

parts.words: Is he the distributor for The Tablet?
parts.note: The Tablet looks like the Catholic weekly paper, but the clue means pills handed out by a pharmacist

explanation.definitionFit: A chemist who makes up prescriptions hands out pills to patients.

clue.text: The Spanish preserved your predecessor in a sort of alcohol

indicators.note: preserved means kept safely inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
thy is the older form that came before 'your'

explanation.surface: A Spaniard keeping an ancestor's body pickled in spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your predecessor' means the older form of the word your, used in archaic English, not an ancestor.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical group found in the ordinary drinking spirit, giving its name to that spirit.

clue.text: Express opinion of one level of VAT?

definitions.meaning: to speak at length, give a speech
goods taxed at nothing are zero-rated

explanation.definitionFit: To speak pompously is to declaim, and the zero band of sales tax could be written as the O rate.

clue.text: Spoils the cup

definitions.meaning: spoils are prizes or loot taken in victory
a cup is a prize awarded to winners

explanation.definitionFit: Both a war prize and a sporting cup are tokens of victory.

clue.text: Do better, not being in pain

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
smart means a sharp stinging pain

explanation.surface: Feeling better because one is no longer suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone by cleverness is to do better than them.

clue.text: Idle talk may disconcert

explanation.definitionFit: Chattering on is prattle-like talk, and to fluster someone is to unnerve them.

clue.text: A Democrat, given the choice, is taking issue

parts.note: an option is a choice

explanation.surface: A politician who, offered alternatives, picks a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking issue' suggests arguing; here issue means offspring, so taking a child into one's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means children, and legally taking on someone else's child as one's own is this process.
